note: FNS 1180.3 is QC reviewer methodology, not caseworker policy. The entire section describes how a QC reviewer must evaluate child support deductions using a Comparison I/II framework: verify the amount actually paid (Comparison I), correct the worksheet figure for worker errors or unprocessed changes (Comparison II), and use the corrected figure in the 'error determination process.' This is audit procedure — it tells reviewers how to identify and classify errors, not workers how to process cases. The underlying caseworker-relevant policy (child support deduction eligibility, verification requirements, BEACON entry procedures, updating expense records when circumstances change) is thoroughly covered in the OLG's 'Child Support Expenses Deduction' pages, including verification of legal obligation and payment, BEACON data entry steps ('Entering Child Support Expenses Data > Update a Support Expense Record'), and specific change scenarios (UC ending, earnings ending). The Layer 1 concern about 'reported but unprocessed changes' describes a QC error-finding scenario, not a distinct policy requirement — the general obligation to process reported changes is a fundamental principle covered across OLG change-processing guidance, not something unique to child support.
